questions.q: What is a 1-second decision in Goggins's terms?
a: Choosing to stand and fight instead of giving in
Winning a contest within a single second
Waiting a second before replying in anger
Setting a timer for one second of focus
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the one-second decision is simply the choice to stand up and keep fighting.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by refusing low-level success?
a: Don't get stuck at a level far below your reach
Never accept any promotion at work
Avoid earning more money than you need
Quit whenever a project gets difficult
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns against settling into a level of success much lower than the heights you can reach.

questions.q: How did Alex Hormozi escape his plateau?
a: He licensed his gym system instead of opening more sites
He cut his prices to attract more members
He sold the gym chain to a competitor
He hired more staff for each location
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he licensed his system to other gym chains, moving revenue from six figures to millions.

questions.q: Why is delivering exactly what was asked a mistake at a new job?
a: You blend in and delay your first promotion
Managers will see you as too ambitious
The work will take longer than expected
Colleagues will resent your efficiency
questions.why: Lesson 3 says doing only what is expected makes you invisible among the masses and pushes promotion away.

questions.q: What does Goggins mean by setting your own standards?
a: You decide the level and pace you perform at
You follow the toughest rules you can find
You compare yourself to the best in your field
You let your manager set every target
questions.why: Lesson 3 says choosing your own level raises the bar while letting you work at your own pace.
